question: A virology student is asked to identify a sample of virus. When subjected to a nonionic detergent, which disrupts lipid membranes, the virus was shown to lose infectivity. The student then purified the genetic material from the virus and subjected it to treatment with DNase, an enzyme that cleaves the phosphodiester linkages in the DNA backbone. A minute amount of the sample was then injected into a human cell line and was found to produce viral particles a few days later. Which of the following viruses was in the unknown sample?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: Nonionic detergent disrupts lipid membrane of virus -> Virus loses infectivity -> Genetic material purified -> DNase treatment cleaves DNA backbone -> Sample injected into human cell line -> Viral particles produced a few days later -> Herpesvirus -> 95%

CHAIN: Nonionic detergent disrupts lipid membrane of virus -> Virus loses infectivity -> Genetic material purified -> DNase treatment cleaves DNA backbone -> Sample injected into human cell line -> Viral particles produced a few days later -> Adenovirus -> 90%
analysis: The virus in the unknown sample is likely an adenovirus. Adenoviruses have a nonenveloped capsid structure that can be disrupted by nonionic detergents. Additionally, adenoviruses contain double-stranded DNA as their genetic material, which is susceptible to DNase treatment. The ability of the sample to produce viral particles in a human cell line further supports the characteristics of adenoviruses.
